explanation: Record every distinct node reachable from the first head, stopping at null or a repeated reference. Traverse the second list under the same cycle guard and return the first reference also reachable from the first list. Comparing references avoids confusing equal values with overlap.
timeComplexity: O(m+n), counting distinct reachable nodes Each distinct node is visited once in each reachable set; hash operations are expected O(1).
spaceComplexity: O(m+n) Each guard set can retain every distinct node of its list.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The first traversal records every distinct node reachable from the first head, including its cycle if present. The second traversal checks every distinct reachable node until termination or repetition. An identity in both traversals is exactly an overlapping node; if none exists, the reachable sets are disjoint.
walkthrough: The first prefix [1,2] and second prefix [3] share tail [8,9]. Link each tail back to shared node 8 to make a shared cycle. The second traversal first finds shared node 8 and returns that actual reference. The executable case’s true result is the judge adapter verdict; the callable returns the tree/node/list of moves/random sample described above.
edgeCases: Only one cyclic list cannot overlap an acyclic list.
Equal values in separate nodes do not establish overlap.
A repeated-node guard is required for both traversals.
